turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, give me one minute, your file is not opening. This computer is very slow today.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): I am sitting only in that corridor for forty minutes. I am tired, and my chest is tight. What is the point of this delay.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): The queue is heavy, I know. What is troubling you today?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): This cough. Every morning I am coughing like anything, and when I climb the stairs to the flat I am short of breath. I cannot manage it anymore.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long has the cough been there?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): The breathing gets worse after I walk to the bus stop, and the dust on the road is too much in the morning. I have started avoiding that side.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, that is not what I asked. How long has the cough itself been going on? Say that again, I lost my place.

[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh. The morning cough is there from many years. It became much worse after the chest infection, three weeks or maybe one month, I don't remember the date exactly. I am not writing it down anywhere.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): One second, the screen jumped. You are saying a chest infection recently, yes?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. Fever was there, the clinic doctor gave an antibiotic. Fever settled. The cough did not go, still every morning, with white sticky phlegm.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever now? Any blood in that phlegm?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever now. No blood also. It is just white and sticky, mostly in the morning.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest pain? Swelling of the legs?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain. Legs are not swollen. I am not sleeping though, the cough wakes me around five, and then I am irritable the whole day. What to do.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): About ten a day... well, actually maybe twenty. Since my twenties, some thirty-five years. You will write it, so what is the use of hiding.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Say the number again please. The cursor moved out of the box. How many cigarettes in a day?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Mostly twenty. If I am busy in the shop, sometimes less. Count it as twenty, don't make me repeat.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any diabetes or blood pressure? The problem list on this screen looks mixed up.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): That metformin is my wife's. She has sugar, she takes metformin five hundred morning and night. I don't have sugar. Last time they told me my pressure is normal.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, so the metformin is hers, not yours. Which medicines are you yourself taking?

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Inhalers only. The blue one is salbutamol, two puffs when the chest is tight. The brown one they said morning and night, but I use it when I remember, maybe three times in a week. I forget, I am tired of all this.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): The brown inhaler, what name is on it? Tell me again, I had opened the wrong tab.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Beclomethasone. Two hundred. Two puffs morning and night is what is written. I am not doing it like that, I already said.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the antibiotic for that infection, are you still taking it?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Amoxicillin. Five days, three times a day. The course is finished, I stopped last week. No tablets now.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to medicines?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me listen to the chest. Big breath in... and out. There is wheeze on both sides. I am not hearing any crackles.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): It feels tight inside, yes. Can we finish soon, I want to go and lie down.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Vitals are up on the screen, I will read them. Blood pressure 136 over 82, pulse 92, oxygen saturation 94 percent, respiratory rate 20.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): 94 is low, no? I knew the stairs were not just in my head.

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): A little low for sitting quietly. Spirometry was done this morning, let me read it before this window closes. FEV1 is 1.8 litres, 62 percent predicted. FVC is 3.1 litres. The ratio is 58 percent.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Simple words, please. I did not follow half of that, my head is heavy from no sleep.

[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): The airways are narrowed. My working impression is COPD from the long smoking, not a final diagnosis, but the numbers fit. It could also be leftover from that chest infection, though the cough for years points more to COPD.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): So now it is oxygen, like my neighbour? I am fed up of this kind of talk.

[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): No oxygen today. Smoking is the part we can still change. I am offering you quitting support with the cessation clinic. They can start nicotine replacement if you are willing.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): I will think. Cold turkey I cannot do. Don't lecture me, I already know twenty is too much, and I am irritable enough.

[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will refer you to that clinic. Please also use the beclomethasone every day, two puffs in the morning and two at night, not only when you remember. Salbutamol when you are breathless, maximum four times in a day.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Every day the brown one, fine, I will try. My sister keeps biotin and she said take the same for hair fall. I told her nonsense, that bottle is hers.

[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Leave the biotin, it is not your medicine and it will not help the lungs. If the breathlessness suddenly gets worse, or the fever comes back, or you see blood, don't wait, come back.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): And the morning cough, it will come down or I just have to live with it.

[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): It can ease if the smoking reduces and the inhaler is taken daily, but not in two days. I want to see you in four weeks. If you are worse before that, come earlier, don't sit at home.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Four weeks is okay. Last time somebody talked of a chest x-ray and nothing happened. Are you actually doing it, or only talking.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will book the chest x-ray, so we are not missing anything else after that infection. Ask at the desk on the way out, they will have the form.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Good. Is there more? I am exhausted, that corridor was too much.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): That is all. Inhalers as I said, the quitting referral, the x-ray, and a review in four weeks. Any questions?
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Just make the morning cough less. That is the only thing I want.

spec.situation: Long-term smoker with morning cough and breathlessness; minimises smoking ('about ten a day... maybe twenty'), inhalers used irregularly, a recent chest infection; spirometry numbers read aloud; quitting support offered.
features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Wife having sugar is not family history and concerns another person.

omissions.text: Current hypertension was asked about and denied: patient said his blood pressure was normal last time they checked.
Recent chest infection timing/details not fully captured: cough became much worse after a chest infection about 3 weeks to 1 month ago, and the patient had fever then which settled after antibiotics.
White sticky phlegm is mostly in the morning.
